Title: GiatMARA instructor killed, 2 children injured in Alza-lorry crash in Sabah
Article:
KOTA BELUD: A GiatMARA instructor was killed and her two teenage children were injured after Perodua Alza car collided with a lorry along Jalan Kota Belud-Tuaran near Taman Nikmat.
Norasida Mayur, 42, died at the scene after being pinned in the driver's seat of the vehicle in the 11.05am crash.
Kota Belud police chief Superintendent Khairul Shah Peri said preliminary investigations showed the lorry, driven by a 42-year-old man, was heading from Kota Belud towards Tuaran.
He said the victim's car, carrying her three children aged between 15 and 18, was travelling in the opposite direction.
"Upon reaching the location, the Perodua Alza is believed to have entered the oncoming lane, resulting in the collision.
"The impact caused the car to spin around and face towards Tuaran, while the lorry came to a stop near a roadside eatery," he said when contacted.
Khairul said the victim's body was sent to the Kota Belud Hospital forensic unit for further action.
Two of her children, aged 15 and 18, suffered injuries and were taken to Kota Belud Hospital for treatment. Her 17-year-old child escaped unhurt.
The lorry driver was also uninjured and has been detained to assist in investigations.
Khairul urged eyewitnesses or anyone with information on the incident to contact the Kota Belud district police headquarters Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.

Title: Algae growth turns Pertang River green, says Fisheries Dept
Article:
SEREMBAN: Excessive algae growth caused by prolonged hot weather and a lack of rainfall has turned the river water in Mukim Pertang, Jelebu, green.
The Negri Sembilan Department of Fisheries (DOF) director Kasim Tawe said investigations found the colour change was not caused by pollution, but by green algae growth in nearby fish ponds due to the hot weather.
"The DOF has taken the initiative to monitor the area, as green algae growth in fish ponds can have either positive or negative effects depending on the density and species of fish.
"This algae does not pose a danger to fish and, under controlled conditions, provides dissolved oxygen and serves as a natural food source, while helping to improve water quality," he said today.
Kasim said algae also acts as a natural shield against the sun's rays, helping to reduce stress on fish.
However, he said uncontrolled algae growth could cause dissolved oxygen levels to fall rapidly, particularly at night, as well as trigger sudden fluctuations in water pH, potentially clogging fish gills.
Kasim said fish breeders should take several measures to control algae growth, including using waterwheels at night, changing the water gradually, reducing feeding, installing shading nets, applying probiotics, and reducing the fish population in the ponds.
He said the Jelebu police and the Jelebu District Fisheries Office would continuously monitor the river and fish ponds to keep the situation under control.
The former mining pond covers approximately 29.54 hectares and is used to breed baung, red tilapia, and Lee Koh fish.
The clarification follows a viral WhatsApp message claiming the change in the river water colour was caused by water discharge from nearby fish-breeding ponds. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Madinah: Different audit methods led to contrasting AG, PwC findings on TH
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former auditor general Tan Sri Dr Madinah Mohamad has defended the audit of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), saying its findings differed from a subsequent PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) review because the two used different methodologies.
She said the audit was conducted under the Audit Act and Tabung Haji Act, with the objective of determining whether TH's financial statements presented a true and fair view in accordance with the Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS), particularly MFRS 139.
In contrast, she said PwC's review was conducted as a "Financial Position Review", a special assignment with different terms of reference and a broader approach to assessing TH's financial position.
This included a different approach to recognising impairment compared with a statutory audit, she said.
"These differences in methodology and approach resulted in the two reports producing different figures, which has often been raised.
"The audited financial statements showed a net profit of about RM3.4 billion, while PwC's Financial Position Review reported a deficit or loss of about RM1.4 billion.
"The difference was due to differences in methodology and the approach to recognising asset impairment and valuing investments, particularly involving subsidiaries and associates as well as investment assets," she said at the Musyawarah Nasional 2.0 Forum – Reality and Perception: Don't Politicise TH.
Madinah said the Financial Reporting Standards Implementation Committee (FRSIC) Consensus 14 should also be assessed in its proper context.
She said PwC had used it as a basis for adjustments to TH's financial statements in documents submitted to the Malaysian Institute of Accountants (MIA).
"This is because there are differing professional views on the suitability of applying FRSIC Consensus 14 in the context of TH.
"However, a letter from the MIA chief executive officer clarified that FRSIC Consensus 14 is not an MFRS with mandatory force like the financial reporting standards issued by the Malaysian Accounting Standards Board (MASB).
"Instead, it is consensus-based guidance to assist in applying standards in certain circumstances.
"But can its use be accepted in the context of a statutory body such as TH?" she said.
Her remarks come after a 211-page Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report
found that weaknesses
in TH's accounting practices resulted in the institution recording a RM3.4 billion profit in 2017 when it should have reported a RM1.4 billion loss.
The RCI said TH's financial position was significantly weaker than disclosed, with its findings supporting key aspects of PwC's independent financial review, which found that the institution had been operating with an asset-liability deficit since 2014.
The report said the discrepancy was partly due to weaknesses in accounting practices, including the failure to recognise impairment losses on investments in subsidiaries, associated companies and fixed-income instruments.
It also found that TH had not fully accounted for declines in the fair value of investment properties and had declared hibah for the 2017 financial year without taking into account the full extent of impairment losses.
The commission said TH had also recorded dividend income from subsidiaries that had not been received, contributing to an overstated financial position.

Title: #NSTviral: Johor-Singapore bus driver braves rain to confront queue-cutting motorists [WATCH]
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A Johor-Singapore bus driver braved heavy rain to confront several motorists who allegedly cut the queue and used a dedicated bus lane to overtake other vehicles at the Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) Complex here.
Bus drivers plying the Johor Baru-Singapore Causeway daily often honk continuously in frustration when motorists use the dedicated bus lane to jump the queue before cutting back into the line heading towards the Bangunan Sultan Ismail CIQ.
However, one driver took a different approach.

Title: Elderly woman allegedly killed over home renovation fee dispute
Article:
SANDAKAN: A dispute over a home renovation fee allegedly led to the murder of a 62-year-old woman, whose body was found dumped in a toilet at her house in Jalan Leila, Tanah Merah.
The victim, who lived alone, had hired her neighbour to renovate her house but reportedly refused to pay the amount demanded by the suspect, sparking a dispute.
The suspect allegedly assaulted and strangled the woman before dumping her body in the toilet, according to a source.
The source said neighbours noticed a foul stench coming from the house several days later and notified the police at 8pm last Wednesday.
"An inspection inside the house led to the discovery of the body with its hands tied behind its back with rope and its head covered with a cloth. The victim is believed to have been dead for several days based on the decomposed state of the body.
"Of the 10 arrests made, two main suspects have been identified," the source said.
Sandakan police chief Assistant Commissioner George Abd Rakman confirmed that 10 people aged between 10 and 39, including three Filipinos, were detained.
He said they were arrested within 24 hours of the body's discovery, and all are believed to be related.
"Police seized a wooden stick believed to have been used in the incident, as well as several personal belongings belonging to the victim that were stolen by the suspect.
"Investigations are ongoing, and the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Marang Prison inmate beaten to death by 3 prisoners over old debt
Article:
MARANG: A 38-year-old inmate at Marang Prison was beaten to death yesterday by three prisoners over a dispute.
Marang police chief Superintendent Sofian Redzuan said the victim was brought to the Merchang health clinic for treatment but was confirmed dead on arrival.
The body was then taken to Hospital Sultanah Nur Zahirah in Kuala Terengganu for a post-mortem.
"The autopsy confirmed the cause of death was a ruptured spleen resulting from blunt force trauma, such as punches or kicks," Sofian said.
He said three inmates, aged 21, 35 and 35, were identified as the suspects who attacked and beat the victim.
Initial investigations revealed that the incident stemmed from an old debt and lingering dissatisfaction among the suspects towards the victim.
Sofian said the case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, and further investigations were underway before the three suspects were brought to court.
The offence carries the death penalty or a jail term of 30 to 40 years with a minimum of 12 strokes of the rotan.

Title: Man arrested over theft, burning of Quran copies in Senawang
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police arrested a man at a hotel in Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur, yesterday to assist in investigations into the theft and burning of copies of the Quran.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the 25-year-old suspect was arrested following a public complaint about a fire near a field in Senawang on Aug 22.
"Investigations revealed that the fire involved several copies of the Quran. Police later received a report at 4.45pm the same day regarding the theft of copies from a mosque in Forest Heights here.
"The suspect was subsequently arrested at 9.30pm last night during a raid at a hotel in Chow Kit," he said in a statement today.
He said police found two bags containing 16 copies of the Quran during a search of the hotel room, and seized three mobile phones as well as the suspect's personal belongings.
Alzafny said all the copies recovered from the suspect were believed to have been taken without permission from mosques and surau in the Chow Kit area.
"We are not ruling out the possibility that some of the copies were taken from a university in the north, following the discovery of the university's ownership stamp.
"A search was also conducted at the suspect's family home in Senawang on the same day, resulting in the seizure of 36 Quran covers from his room," he said.
Alzafny said initial investigations found a link between the suspect and the Quran-burning incident on Aug 22, with the case being investigated under Sections 380 and 295 of the Penal Code.
He said checks revealed that the suspect had four previous criminal records and had just completed a two-month police supervision order.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Putin allows Russia to take control of infrastructure deemed vulnerable to drone attacks
Article:
MOSCOW: President Vladimir Putin on Monday handed the Russian state the power to take control of critically important infrastructure if it is deemed to be poorly protected from Ukrainian drone attacks and other threats.
The special powers, set out in a presidential decree, will allow the state to take over temporary administration of such facilities at a time when Ukraine has stepped up drone attacks on oil refineries and retail warehouses.
The state will be able to take control of physical and financial assets and formal ownership rights if entities responsible for such facilities are judged to have failed in their duty to protect them and are too slow to repair them after any attack, according to the decree.
It applies to fuel, energy, industrial, communications, transport and logistics facilities and other objects regarded as critically-important for ensuring the security and economic stability of the state and the population.
First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov said the measure should not be viewed as a precursor to nationalisation and would not be used on a broad scale.
"This does not involve nationalisation or a change of ownership. The decree provides for the state to take part in managing an enterprise in order to address specific security issues," Manturov was quoted as saying by Interfax.
Putin last week ordered the government to launch a programme to rebuild commercial warehouses damaged or destroyed by Ukraine in recent weeks.
Kyiv has attacked at least two dozen warehouses belonging to Russia's top online retailer Wildberries since July 18, destroying a large chunk of its storage capacity.
On Monday, Russia's second-largest online retailer Ozon, said four of its logistics hubs in southern Russia had been targeted in Ukrainian attacks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore reaffirm commitment to keep key straits safe
Article:
SINGAPORE: Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore have reaffirmed their shared commitment to keeping the Straits of Malacca and Singapore free, open and safe for international shipping.
The commitment was made by the Malaysia Marine Department, Indonesia's Directorate General of Sea Transportation and the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) in a joint statement issued during the 17th Co-operation Forum today.
They underscored the importance of respecting navigational rights and freedoms, both in principle and in practice, affirming that the waterways are "straits used for international navigation", where the right of transit passage applies under the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and customary international law.
Meanwhile, Singapore Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow said the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (SOMS) were a primary artery for global trade, with more than 100,000 vessels passing through the waterways each year.
He said the straits carried almost a quarter of global seaborne trade and almost a third of the world's oil and gas supplies.
"Events in West Asia this year reminded the world that open sea lanes can never be taken for granted.
"In our part of the world, we will endeavour to keep the Straits of Malacca and Singapore free, open and safe for international shipping," he said during the opening of the forum.
Siow noted that the Cooperative Mechanism, formalised in 2007, was the first and remains the only implementation of Article 43 of UNCLOS, which calls on countries to cooperate on navigational safety and pollution prevention.
Through the Cooperative Mechanism, countries have turned shared interests into collective action in three key areas: anticipating risks early, regularly upgrading infrastructure and responding collectively to incidents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fire crews gain ground on destructive blaze raging near Reno, Nevada
Article:
RENO: Firefighters logged major gains on Monday against a wind-driven blaze that threatened the city of Reno, Nevada, over the weekend, destroying dozens of houses and chasing tens of thousands of people from their homes.
As of Monday, fire crews had managed to carve containment lines around 27 per cent of the Hawk Fire, which erupted on Saturday near Nevada's third-most-populous city and raced through tinder-dry grass, brush and forest into residential areas.
Within 48 hours, the blaze had scorched more than 6,070 hectares on the outskirts of Reno, a hub of high-tech industry, gambling and outdoor resorts in the eastern foothills of the Sierra Nevada mountain range near the California border.
It was the second major wildfire to strike Nevada's Truckee River valley area in recent weeks.
No fatalities have been reported, but four civilians and three emergency personnel suffered minor burns in the initial hours of the blaze on Saturday, authorities said.
Chief Richard Edwards of the Truckee Meadows Fire Protection District told a press conference that at least 32 homes had gone up in flames, with a half dozen more damaged.
The tally of property losses is expected to climb as damage-assessment teams canvass more of the fire zone in the coming days, he said.
Among the ill-fated property owners was Luke Opperman, 47, a civil engineer who lost his family's home of nearly 20 years when flames swept their suburban Reno neighbourhood.
Opperman, who was away camping at the time, said his wife and two teenage daughters hastily packed up three cars and two trailers with clothes, vital belongings and the family's chickens, goats, dog and cats, then sped off to safety as the fire closed in around them.
The outpouring of support from co-workers and friends, some of whom had already started a GoFundMe page for his family, was overwhelming, Opperman recalled.
"That's what made me break down," he said.
Devastation to the area as a whole was staggering, he said, with six of his neighbours also losing their homes.
He estimated as many as 20 houses had burned up in his immediate community, which lies adjacent to the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest.
"It's more than just a house; it's your neighbourhood, it's your community," Opperman told Reuters, his voice cracking with emotion, in a telephone interview, adding he had yet to fully contemplate what happens next.
"I think it's baby steps," he said. "I don't know what's happening at the end of this week."
As the fire raged out of control over the weekend, wind-whipped flames roared up canyon slopes and over fire trucks while authorities issued evacuation notices urging an estimated 90,000 residents to leave their homes immediately or get set to flee.
By Monday afternoon, the fire threat had diminished enough for officials to lift evacuations in some areas, but Sheriff Darin Balaam said 23,000 residents were still displaced under "go-now" orders, with another 40,000 advised to be ready to go at a moment's notice.
More than 900 firefighters remained assigned to the Hawk Fire on Monday, Edwards said, including personnel from 15 US states as well as crews from Australia and New Zealand who were part of teams dispatched from abroad to help battle dozens of blazes raging across the Western US in recent weeks.
Officials said the Hawk Fire was human-caused, but whether it was intentionally set or ignited by accident remained under investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sunway founder confirms Sunway Lagoon roller coaster incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Group founder Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah has confirmed Saturday night's roller coaster accident at Sunway Lagoon.
"It's an incident that all of us regret very much. We are lucky that there were no fatalities," Cheah told the New Straits Times.
He said authorities were investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.
"In my view, the incident may be attributable to metal fatigue," Cheah said, adding that police had ruled out foul play.
He also disclosed that the ride had been temporarily closed for comprehensive inspection and maintenance work about two to three weeks before the incident.
Ten people were injured in the accident at Sunway Lagoon on Saturday night.
The incident occurred at about 9pm and involved 22 riders, comprising Malaysians and foreign tourists aged between 11 and 44.
Yesterday, Subang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said 10 riders suffered minor injuries.
He, however, did not name the theme park in question.
The incident came to light after a video circulated on social media showing a woman being carried down a flight of stairs on a stretcher near a section of the roller coaster track surrounded by trees.
A second video, recorded during the day, showed a crowd gathered near the amusement ride area, while several police personnel and theme park staff were seen walking away from one of the rides.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm, heavy rain warning for 10 states, 3 Federal Territories
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds across 10 states and three Federal Territories until 5pm today.
The Federal Territories affected are Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, and Labuan.
In Peninsular Malaysia, the affected states comprise Perlis, Kedah, Penang, and Selangor (Kuala Selangor, Klang, Kuala Langat, Petaling, Gombak, Sepang, and Hulu Langat).
Also affected are Perak (Kerian, Larut Matang, Selama, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Muallim, Batang Padang, Kampar, and Kinta); Pahang (Bera, Rompin, Kuantan, Cameron Highlands, Maran, and Pekan); Negri Sembilan (Jempol and Jelebu); and Johor (Segamat).
In Sarawak, the alert covers Mukah (Mukah), Miri, Bintulu, Sibu (Selangau and Kanowit), Limbang, Kuching (Kuching and Bau), Sarikei (Julau), and Kapit (Belaga).
In Sabah, the areas involved are the Interior (Kuala Penyu, Beaufort, Membakut, Keningau, Tambunan, Tenom, and Sipitang), West Coast (Papar, Putatan, Penampang, Kota Kinabalu, and Tuaran), and Sandakan (Kinabatangan).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN, Umno call for new RCI to investigate TH
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional has called for a new Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) to be established to reinvestigate Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said this was necessary as findings from the previous RCI report on TH had been used to manipulate the narrative and portray the agency as having been embroiled in a major financial scandal.
He claimed that the issue now was the alleged manipulation of information concerning TH, which he said had been exaggerated to portray the country's Islamic financial institution as being in serious financial trouble.
Takiyuddin also claimed there were factual errors during the Dewan Rakyat's winding-up session to debate the RCI on TH by the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, giving the impression that he did not fully understand issues concerning the agency.
"We do not deny that there may have been technical errors that can be rectified, but these should not be used as an attack to portray TH as having been embroiled in such a major scandal.
"I agree with the forum participants' proposal for the RCI on TH to be re-established to investigate TH's position from 2018 to date.
"Therefore, the government is urged to establish a new RCI into the administration and management of TH, beginning from the end of the previous RCI's period up to now," said the PAS secretary-general.
Takiyuddin, who is also the Kota Baru member of parliament, said this at a press conference after attending the Musyawarah Nasional 2.0 Forum - Reality and Perception: Don't Politicise TH, here today.
Also present were Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Wanita Umno chief Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad, Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi and Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
Meanwhile, Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Mohd Razlan Rafii also supported the establishment of a new RCI to investigate TH's financial affairs after the previous RCI.
He said the move was aimed at determining whether there had been any elements of misconduct or the sale of assets to interested parties.
"The government is responsible for conducting an investigation and taking appropriate action against those responsible.
"We also need to know the status of TH assets that were transferred and how they generated profits, as well as why they were not returned to TH," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Slight haze relief as unhealthy areas drop from 32 to 29
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nationwide haze conditions showed slight improvement, with 29 areas recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2.30pm today, compared with 32 areas this morning.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the highest reading was recorded at the Serian district police headquarters monitoring station in Sarawak at 182.
This was followed by Johan Setia (173), Sri Aman (170), Shah Alam (162) and Kuching (160).
Other locations registering unhealthy levels include Tanjung Malim with 157; Minden (156); Samarahan  (156); Taiping (155); Tasek Ipoh (155); Putrajaya (155); and Bukit Rambai (155).
The Batu Muda monitoring station in Kuala Lumpur recorded a reading of 154, followed by Nilai (154); Sungai Petani (153); Pegoh Ipoh (153); Kuala Selangor(153); and Sarikei (153).
Additionally, Seberang Perai recorded a reading of 152, as well as Seri Manjung, Petaling Jaya, Seremban, Alor Gajah, Segamat, Batu Pahat and Tangkak.
Klang recorded 151, followed by Banting (146) and Balik Pulau (139).
Under the API classification, readings of 0 to 50 are considered good, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and above 300 hazardous.
A total of 38 monitoring stations recorded moderate readings, with none registering very unhealthy or hazardous levels.
API data is updated hourly from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Stray elephant in Kampung Jeram relocated to Royal Belum State Park
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A female elephant that had been roaming around Kampung Jeram, Manir, since last Friday was successfully relocated by the Terengganu Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) today.
Its director, Dennis Ten, said the elephant was captured and rescued on Saturday.
He said the relocation operation began at 8am today and involved 13 Terengganu Perhilitan personnel, seven staff from the Sungai Deka Elephant Conservation Centre and two personnel from the National Elephant Conservation Centre in Kuala Gandah.
"The wild elephant was in a safe and stable condition during the relocation process.
"It was then transported to Royal Belum State Park in Perak to be released," he said.
Dennis expressed his appreciation for the support and cooperation of all agencies involved in the elephant relocation operation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Strong winds hamper efforts to battle 51.4ha peat fire in Kota Tinggi
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Hot weather and strong winds are hampering efforts to put out a 51.4-hectare peat fire along Jalan Bypass Sebana Cove-Punggai that broke out yesterday.
Operations commander Deputy Fire Superintendent II Baharuddin Idris said 9.7 per cent of the 35.6-hectare fire in Sector A, as well as the entire 15.8-hectare Sector B, was under control.
"Our main challenges are strong winds, hot weather and limited water supply. We get water using water tankers with the help of related agencies, including Ranhill SAJ.
"No new fires have been detected in the area and there have been no casualties reported," he said when met by reporters at the site today.
Baharuddin said firefighters were using the direct attack method while waiting for two excavators from other agencies, scheduled to arrive at noon.
He said the department needed larger amphibious excavators capable of operating in peat and forest areas to create firebreaks, particularly in Sector A.
Baharuddin said there was a risk of the fire spreading if the winds strengthened, although the situation in Sector B was under control.
"We hope if the weather isn't too hot, we can put out the fire there (Sector B). But in Sector A, we still need help to create firebreaks using amphibious excavators," he said.
The fire was not threatening residential areas, with the nearest housing area in Sebana Cove about three kilometres away, while Punggai was about four to five kilometres from the fire.
The road has been closed to the public since 2pm yesterday.
Baharuddin said the affected area was categorised as agricultural land, with a small part of the surrounding area being an oil palm plantation owned by Keledang Felda, while other areas had yet to be cultivated.
He said the cause of the fire had yet to be determined and investigations were ongoing.
"There are people who enter this area, probably to fish, but we cannot determine if it has any relation to the cause of the fire," he said, adding that 21 personnel, including four Civil Defence Force members, were involved in firefighting efforts.
Meanwhile, Tanjung Surat assemblyman Aznan Tamin advised local residents to follow the authorities' instructions, avoid using the closed Punggai bypass and take alternative routes.
He also advised nearby residents, particularly those in Taman Bayu Damai and Punggai, to wear facemasks if exposed to thick smoke, as the Air Pollution Index (API) reading in the area had risen slightly to 125.
"In light of this incident, I hope everyone will be more cautious and not conduct open burning, especially during hot weather," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PAC to discuss proposal for special body to review TH management tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) will discuss a proposal to establish a special body to review the management of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2017 onwards.
PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the matter would be discussed with committee members after its proceedings in Parliament tomorrow.
"Tomorrow, PAC has proceedings in Parliament. God willing, after the proceedings, I will meet and discuss the proposal to establish this special body with all PAC members," she said when contacted.
Earlier today, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi proposed that the PAC establish a special body to examine the management of TH from 2017 onwards.
Zahid said the move was important to enable the body to establish the true state of affairs concerning TH from 2017 onwards, based on the facts.
He said this would help correct public perception regarding TH's management and governance issues.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan Nazrin honours 82-year-old mother of 15 with family award
Article:
IPOH: Raising 15 children while living a modest life was never easy for Yang Walad, but her faith, patience and prayers helped her see them through to adulthood.
The 82-year-old from Parit Haji Tahir, Parit Buntar, was deeply touched after receiving the Tokoh Keluarga Mithali award in conjunction with the Perak-level Maulidur Rasul 1448H celebrations today.
Yang said she never expected to receive the award, especially from the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah.
"I am deeply touched. I never expected it. I was also very touched when I was told that I would receive the award from the Sultan of Perak himself," she said when met after the ceremony.
She received RM10,000, an Umrah package worth RM9,000 and a plaque at the event.
Recalling the challenges of raising 15 children, Yang said she and her late husband lived a simple life, with her working in the padi fields to support the family.
"I did not come from a well-off family. We lived a simple life. I worked in the padi fields while raising my children.
"Whenever there was sustenance, I made sure my children grew up well. I always had one determination in my heart, I wanted my children to succeed," she said.
Yang said she never stopped praying for her children and believed that faith and perseverance were key to raising them.
"Every day, I would pray to Allah to provide sustenance and help my children succeed. That was my intention," she said, adding that her husband died in 2010 after suffering from diabetes.
Despite becoming a widow, Yang continued raising their children, six boys and nine girls, including a girl with Down syndrome.
She said she has more than 50 grandchildren and more than 10 great-grandchildren.
Sharing her advice with young mothers, Yang said they should have faith in themselves, continuously pray for their children and never give up on them.
"For mothers raising children, especially young mothers, you need to have faith and pray to Allah. You must have confidence that your children can succeed.
"Whenever my children went to school, I would pray and ask Allah to help them succeed. I prayed every day," she said.
She said watching her children progress from school to Form Six and eventually university had been among the most meaningful moments of her life.
Yang's children are mostly educators and civil servants, while some work in the private sector.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid wants PAC to probe management of TH after 2017
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) should establish a special body to investigate the management of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2017 to the present, says Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The deputy prime minister said the move was important to enable the body to clarify the true situation regarding TH after 2017, based on facts.
Zahid said this would help correct public perception regarding TH's management and governance issues.
"This recommendation should be followed to dispel claims of 'sakau'. The certificate issued by the National Audit Department clearly shows that TH's audit was based on the Tabung Haji Act, which provides that the process must be carried out by the department.
"This is what the PAC should examine so that it can correct perceptions," Zahid told a press conference at the Forum Musyawarah Nasional 2.0 on the TH issue.
Separately, Zahid said he had no intention of submitting a proposal raised at the forum for the re-establishment of an RCI to investigate TH.
He said the informal proposal by MPs for the PAC to probe the matter would be a more appropriate way forward.
"On calls for another RCI to be held, I think the PAC is better suited to conduct the investigation because it has locus standi as enshrined in its duties and responsibilities," he said.
Today's forum was attended by a number of top Umno and Pas leaders, including Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and his Pas counterpart Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan.
Earlier, former auditor-general Tan Sri Dr Madinah Mohamad denied that there were elements of
direct theft
at TH during her tenure, which the RCI looked into.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man with disabilities reports loan shark harassment over unpaid loans
Article:
CHERAS: A person with disabilities (PWD) said he has faced almost daily harassment from loan sharks since last month over unpaid loans exceeding RM17,000 taken through money lending apps.
Kong Jun Xian, 24, a PWD under the intellectual disability category, said he took out loans totalling nearly RM4,000 through five apps downloaded after seeing advertisements on social media in June.
He said each loan was subject to a high service transaction fee.
"I took a loan of RM1,900 on one app but only received RM1,100 because they charged a service transaction fee of RM800.
"I didn't expect to be deceived and I want to repay the loan, but I have no money at this time," he said at a press conference at the DAP Socialist Youth (DAPSY) Selangor Complaints Centre here today.
He said unknown individuals suspected to be loan sharks began contacting him from several phone numbers last month to demand repayment, escalating to criminal threats.
"They threatened to burn my house, splash it with red paint and harass my family.
"I also received death threats and photos of these threats.
"I am under stress and worried about my safety and my family's. Even though I said I will repay the money, they still harass me every day," he said.
He has since lodged a police report.
DAPSY Selangor chief Lee Wen Bin said he hoped police would take appropriate action given the criminal threats and that the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) should act against unlicensed money lending advertisements on social media.
"This is the first time I've come across a money lending application and I will lodge a complaint with MCMC so they can take action against the advertisement and application.
"The relevant parties seem to be getting bolder, so the authorities must take early action; otherwise, it is not impossible that others will be deceived," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Miti to drive low-altitude economy development with unmanned valley ecosystem project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry will implement the Unmanned Valley Ecosystem pilot project to drive the development of the low-altitude economy (LAE).
LAE refers to economic activities and public services conducted within a low-altitude airspace ecosystem using technologies such as drones, advanced air mobility, air logistics, infrastructure inspection, smart farming, and emergency services.
The sector also includes unmanned aerial vehicles, air taxis, and vertical take-off and landing electric aircraft.
Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said the project would be carried out under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), with the proposed pilot project to be located at universities.
"The government under the National Aerospace Industry Corporation of Malaysia is planning to establish an 'unmanned valley', where all flights, including the vertiport system, can be tested.
"Rolling out the pilot project at universities will attract the younger generation because, ultimately, they will be the ones to use this technology," he told Bernama after appearing on Bernama TV's Ruang Bicara programme titled "Low-Altitude Economic Development, Digitalisation & Aerospace," on Monday.
Sim, however, said that they are also open to suggestions for other suitable locations to implement the pilot project.
He said the pilot project's implementation must take into account several challenges, especially regarding safety, to ensure the technology can be tested and developed properly.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke previously said the LAE guidelines are expected to be announced by the end of this year, providing a regulatory, operational, and governance framework to ensure safe airspace integration in the sector.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia is developing the guidelines, which are expected to be announced at the Asian Transport Expo 2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kuantan port eyes liquid cargo diversification, to handle 30mil tonnes of liquefied CO2 annually by 2050
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuantan Port Consortium Sdn Bhd has projected liquefied carbon dioxide (CO2) handling to reach five million tonnes per year by 2030 in the first phase, potentially rising to 30 million tonnes per annum by 2050.
Kuantan Port chief commercial officer Mazlim Husin said the port has collaborated with Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) on carbon capture and storage, which could see liquid cargo playing a more important role at the port.
He said Petronas has signed an agreement to lease or sublease about 60 hectares (ha) at Kuantan Port for the development of a terminal.
"We have a collaboration with Petronas at Kuantan Port. There are about 60 ha to be leased or subleased by Petronas from us, in which there's going to be a terminal," he said during the CEO Panel: Ports and Shipping at the LogiSYM Malaysia 2026 conference recently.
"There will be an importation of liquefied CO2, for example, from Japan. And it will be shipped by special vessel from Japan to Kuantan, and discharged into the Petronas terminal," he said.
The CO2 will prepared according to required specifications and pressurised before being transported via a 250 km pipeline to be injected into permanent geological storage sites offshore.
Mazlim said Kuantan Port could foresee that the liquid cargo is going to play a significant role in its future cargo mix.
Beyond imported CO2, Mazlim said Kuantan Port could potentially serve emitters from other parts of Peninsular Malaysia through rail connectivity.
Emitters such as steel mills and cement plants could potentially transport liquefied CO2 by rail from the west coast to Kuantan Port before it is injected into permanent geological storage sites offshore, he said.
Mazlim said Kuantan Port is working closely with Petronas, with the project targeted to be sanctioned for the execution phase next year.
"At the moment, we are working very closely with Petronas.
"By next year, we hope we will come to a final decision and hopefully, it's going to work," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Philippines seeking to expand military drone capabilities, says defence chief
Article:
MANILA: The Philippines plans to expand its unmanned capabilities, including through development and acquisition of drones as part of efforts to modernise its military, its defence chief said on Tuesday.
US defence ally the Philippines also plans to acquire additional guided-missile corvettes and other major defence assets to beef up its external defence capabilities, Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro told a budget hearing in the lower house of Congress.
The Philippines has shifted its security focus from internal threats to external security as tensions rise with Beijing in the South China Sea, where confrontations between them over disputed features inside Manila's exclusive economic zone have grown in frequency in recent years.
The armed forces currently operate a fleet of unmanned aerial vehicles that provide intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, Teodoro said.
"As we mature on the cycle, then we can acquire more," Teodoro said in pitching to lawmakers a 6.3 per cent increase in the defence ministry's budget for 2027, from the 305.5 billion pesos (US$4.95 billion) spending plan approved for this year.
Drone expansion is part of a proposed 50 billion pesos (US$810.4 million) allocation for the Philippines' modernisation programme next year, 25 per cent higher than that of the current budget.
The priority was also developing the systems, connectivity and operational know-how needed to use drones effectively, Teodoro added.
"More than the personnel, it is the integration into the operation, what do you do with them and how do you use them," he said.
Developing secure communications and network capabilities was crucial, he added.
Teodoro declined to identify specific systems under consideration, saying the details were classified and highly sensitive.
"They are very, very sensitive to compromise, particularly with AI," he said, adding that the Philippines was in close contact with several countries with expertise in drone technology.
Yuliia Fediv, Ukraine's ambassador to the Philippines, told Reuters in June that Kyiv has been in discussions with Manila over drone technology cooperation.
In June, the United States said it has given the Philippine military four solar-powered sea drones to boost its maritime surveillance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khee San chairman steps down after six bank accounts frozen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Khee San Bhd's largest shareholder Datuk Seri Ngu Tieng Ung stepped down as executive chairman on Monday due to personal reasons, the company said in a Bursa Malaysia filing.
Ngu holds a 27.18 per cent indirect stake in the confectionery company through his private vehicles, Heritage Winners Sdn Bhd and Juarastasi Amad Sdn Bhd. He also has a 0.01 per cent direct interest in the company.
His resignation came three days after Khee San announced that six bank accounts belonging to its subsidiary Khee San Food Industries Sdn Bhd had been frozen following an investigation under anti-money laundering laws.
In a separate filing, Khee San said the six accounts had an aggregate credit balance of about RM1.89 million at the time they were frozen.
The company said it has yet to receive formal written clarification from the police on the specific circumstances or matters leading to the investigation.
"However, based on information conveyed by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to the company, the freezing of the accounts is not due to or connected with the operations or business activities of the group.
"The company is actively seeking further clarification and information from PDRM in respect of the matter," it said.
Khee San submitted an appeal to the police on Aug 24 to lift the freezing order.
It said the freezing of the accounts had resulted in immediate operational implications, affecting customer receipts and the processing of collections through the affected accounts.
It also affected payments to suppliers and staff salaries through the accounts.
"The extent of any impact on the group's sales and production operations has yet to be confirmed. The group is continuing to assess the operational implications and will provide further updates should there be any material development," it added.
Khee San said the matter is not expected to have a material financial impact on the company at this juncture, although the financial and operational implications remain subject to further assessment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN's partner for Melaka polls may be decided at Aug 28 Umno meet
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional's partner for the upcoming Melaka election may be known after the Umno Supreme Council meeting on Aug 28.
Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said the issue of political cooperation is expected to be among the key items on the agenda.
"We will wait for the Supreme Council meeting on Aug 28. God willing, there will be a good decision for the people of Melaka," he said.
He did not rule out the possibility that BN's coalition partner for the state election could be decided at the meeting.
Previously, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi indicated that the understanding between BN and Perikatan Nasional would continue in Melaka.
At the same time, Pakatan Harapan has formed a committee to discuss cooperation with BN in the state, with election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari entrusted to lead the talks for PH.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia carves premium niche in Asia's digital-infra race – Economist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is carving out a premium niche in Asia's digital-infrastructure race, combining scalable power, connectivity, execution speed, industrial depth and hyperscale capital, says an economist.
Juwai IQI global chief economist Shan Saeed said Malaysia's data-centre boom is beginning to look less like spillover from Singapore and more like a distinct economic strategy.
He said the investment numbers are increasingly macroeconomically consequential and Malaysia already possesses a sizeable digital base.
"Malaysia is also benefiting from a global reallocation of capital towards compute," he said in a statement to Bernama here today.
The Malaysian Investment Development Authority approved RM144.4 billion in data-centre and cloud-computing investments between 2021 and mid-2025.
In the first quarter of 2026 alone, data-centre and cloud-computing investments accounted for RM34.6 billion across 33 projects, equivalent to 88.9 per cent of information-and-communications investment approvals.
Shan said the policy challenge is to convert infrastructure investment into domestic value-added and productivity growth.
He said that because data centres are capital- and power-intensive, their economic dividend depends on the spillovers they create.
These include lower barriers to cloud and artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, stronger cybersecurity and engineering capabilities, semiconductor linkages, advanced cooling, renewable-energy investment, local procurement and higher-skilled employment.
"This is where Malaysia's semiconductor ecosystem provides an additional advantage.
"Digital infrastructure can create a bridge between the country's established electronics manufacturing base and the emerging AI economy, allowing capital deepening to generate broader technology diffusion across manufacturing and services," said Shan.
He added that Southeast Asia now represents roughly half of Asia-Pacific's data-centre capacity under construction, with Malaysia leading the region with 1,039 megawatts (MW) under construction, ahead of Thailand at 859 MW.
Johor alone recorded 1,110 MW of operational capacity, 602 MW under construction and a 3,088 MW development pipeline in the first half of 2026, with its pipeline exceeding Bangkok's 2,084 MW and Jakarta's 1,699 MW.
Shan said grid resilience, renewable-energy supply, water efficiency and regulatory execution will therefore become part of Malaysia's investment proposition.
He added that the risk is that capacity expands faster than domestic value capture.
Therefore, Malaysia must ensure that digital infrastructure crowds in, rather than crowds out, productive investment.
"If that balance is achieved, the payoff extends well beyond server farms. The data-centre cycle can deepen the productive capital stock, accelerate technology diffusion, raise total-factor productivity and strengthen Malaysia's potential growth rate.
"Malaysia is not merely building data centres. It is building the compute infrastructure and potentially the productivity architecture for Asean's next growth cycle," said Shan.
According to the UN Conference on Trade and Development, global greenfield investment in data centres exceeded US$270 billion in 2025, accounting for more than one-fifth of global greenfield investment value, with Malaysia ranked among the top 10 global destinations for data-centre projects.
McKinsey & Co, a global management consulting firm, meanwhile estimated that data centres could require roughly US$6.7 trillion in cumulative global investment by 2030, with AI workloads accounting for around 70 per cent of capacity demand by the end of the decade.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2017 audit found no direct theft at TH, says former auditor general
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Sri Dr Madinah Mohamad has denied that there were elements of direct theft at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) during her tenure as auditor general.
She said the 2017 Auditor General's Report did not identify any evidence of direct theft at TH when the document was prepared by her and her team.
The former education ministry secretary-general said she would have been the first to lodge a report with the authorities if there had been evidence of direct theft at the agency during the period covered by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI).
"I did not see any such evidence (of theft at TH) when I was the auditor general.
"Rest assured, I would not only have not concealed it, but would have taken it seriously and reported it to the authorities if my team and I had found evidence (of theft at TH).
"The audit was conducted according to standards and based on audit evidence before the statements or certificates were issued. We followed the facts and evidence and remained grounded in reality," she said at the Musyawarah Nasional 2.0 Forum - Reality and Perception: Don't Politicise TH, here today.
Her remarks come after the 211-page RCI report criticised the lack of firmness on the part of the auditor general in relation to TH's financial statements.
The report noted that TH's financial statements from 2014 to 2017 received unqualified audit opinions, although the 2017 audit report contained an Emphasis of Matter (EOM).
Madinah said she was prepared to explain the basis of the audit decisions if she had been called before the commission.
Madinah, who served as Auditor General from 2017 to 2019, previously revealed that she had already been at the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) office when the RCI proceedings were taking place, but her name was not called.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CAP urges action over erosion, pollution at Penang beach
Article:
BAYAN LEPAS: A consumer watchdog has called for immediate action over coastal erosion and marine pollution affecting Tanjung Asam beach in Gertak Sanggul.
Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) president Mohideen Abdul Kader said a recent survey found significant changes to the beach over the past year, including toppled trees, damaged shelters and increasingly polluted seawater.
He said the beach, once known for its clean, clear waters and white sand, was now affected by polluted seawater and blackened sand.
"The coastal area is being battered by increasingly powerful waves, while rising sea levels have caused seawater to reach the main public access road to the beach," he said today.
Mohideen urged the Penang government, Penang Island City Council and relevant departments and agencies to conduct a comprehensive investigation to determine the root cause of the erosion.
He said CAP believed the problem could be linked to a nearby land reclamation project, which may have altered sea currents and caused waves to surge back towards the Tanjung Asam coastline.
"CAP is concerned that if this problem is proven to stem from the land reclamation project, more serious environmental consequences will arise in the future should the issue be allowed to persist without effective resolution," he added.
He called on the state government to publicly disclose the findings of investigations and studies conducted into the matter, as well as measures being taken to address the erosion and pollution.
It was reported that coastal erosion was damaging Tanjung Asam beach, a fishing village on Penang island's southwestern coast, with parts of its shoreline defence and public facilities at risk.
The beach, once known for its clean sand, has gradually been eroded by strong waves, while sections of the shoreline deSfence have collapsed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trees 'giving up': Climate change hammers historic English gardens
Article:
AT Hampton Court Palace, head gardener Graham Dillamore strode across the burnt beige grass in the spectacular formal gardens southwest of London, laid out in the 17th century.
"If we have a summer like this next year, by God, it's going to be a struggle," said Dillamore, who has spent more than 20 years tending the gardens of the Baroque and Tudor red-brick palace where King Henry VIII once caroused.
Created by master designers such as Lancelot "Capability" Brown and William Kent, the gardens of stately homes such as Hampton Court, Blenheim Palace, and Chatsworth House are among England's top visitor attractions.
But their historic style of planting and ancient trees are being hammered by climate change – including record heatwaves and drought this summer.
Gardeners told AFP they were not embarrassed by straw-like lawns – feeling visitors, also facing water restrictions, are understanding – but the concern is for the long-term consequences and keeping the spirit of their gardens alive.
Mature trees that take decades to establish are drooping, and some have leaves turning brown in August in a stress reaction to excessive heat.
"Some of these trees have actually given up. They're not going to come back, they're finished," said Dillamore, who also oversees gardens at Kensington Palace, the official London residence of Prince William and his wife, Catherine.
"We're losing mature tree stock and that's tragic in a historic garden."
"We've already lost trees," said Rosie Fyles, head of gardens at Chiswick House in west London, whose Kent-designed shady lawns dotted with statues and cedars of Lebanon date back to the 18th century.
Suffering most are trees "we really associate with an English garden or an English landscape", she said: oaks, sycamores, birch, limes.
[[nid:1518468]]
"I think there's only so much stress they can withstand," said the gardener, who tends 1,800 trees.
It is not practicable to water mature trees, gardeners explained.
At Chiswick, staff were watering drooping camellias and lilacs, shrubs that normally thrive in sun.
The garden has boosted its capacity to harvest rainwater, but its stocks ran out several months ago.
"There's only so much we can intervene and control," said Fyles, admitting this was hard to accept as a professional gardener.
"It's sobering. It means that we're having to think about what we plant going forward, what trees will be sustainable going forward in the future climate."
"I get the feeling we're in uncharted territory," said Dillamore.
"I've never felt so uncertain about the future in historic gardens and landscapes as I do now."
Staff at historic gardens surveyed by the National Lottery Heritage Fund earlier this year all said climate change was having an impact – not just drought, but also heavy storms and excessive rain in winter that spawns fungus and bugs.
Historic gardens are "really on the front line of climate change", said Drew Bennellick, the Heritage Fund's head of lands, seas and nature policy, and "the changes are happening actually quite quickly now."
"We've seen sites that lost 80 per cent of their tree cover," he told AFP.
Climate modelling by researchers at the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew, a Unesco World Heritage site, predicted that by 2090, 50 per cent of their trees will be at risk of death.
[[nid:1518467]]
Historic gardens "must be protected and preserved", said Dillamore.
"But they've also got to change over the next few years – otherwise we're going to lose them."
And this calls for "some very, very difficult decisions", he admitted.
Some are shifting to Mediterranean plants, Bennellick said, "more grasses, more herbaceous perennials that can survive the drought conditions."
At Hampton Court, Dillamore pointed to vibrant pink flowers with bright green foliage.
Garden designer Ann-Marie Powell created test beds of long-lived plants happy in high temperatures, including Siskiyou Pink plants, native to the southern United States.
Planted in April, they look vigorous despite no automatic irrigation, as do other flowers such as daisy-like echinaceas from US prairies.
Dillamore said he was happy with the result.
Hampton Court and Chiswick have also stopped digging over flowerbeds and relaxed about weeds.
The Royal Horticultural Society gardening charity announced this month it is considering moving some of its heat-stressed hydrangea collection from Surrey, southwest of London, to other regions of England.
"The gardens tell the story of Hampton Court just as much as the palace, so I can't pack this garden up and move it," said Dillamore.
"We've got to retain that feel, the spirit of the place."
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dayang earnings poised to rebound in FY27 after weak FY26
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dayang Enterprise Holdings Bhd is expected to see a rebound in core earnings in financial year 2027 (FY27) and FY28 after a slowdown in its first-half (1H) FY26 performance.
AmInvestment Bank Bhd said Dayang's core earnings of RM54.8 million for 1H FY26 missed expectations, accounting for 24 per cent of its full-year estimate and 30 per cent of consensus estimates.
"While we had anticipated softer activity year-on-year, the slowdown was more severe than expected," it said in a note.
Marine charter pre-tax earnings plunged 82 per cent as Perdana swung to an RM8.4 million loss, while Dayang's topside maintenance services profit fell 30 per cent on slower work order conversion.
The firm cut its earnings forecasts by 50 per cent for FY26 and 12 per cent for FY27, adopting more conservative conversion assumptions.
"Conversely, we raise FY28 forecast by four per cent as we expect vessel utilisation to improve.
"Following the FY26 reset, we project core earnings to rebound by 102 per cent in FY27 and 23 per cent in FY28, implying a 58 per cent two-year compound annual growth rate over FY26 through FY28," it said.
AmInvestment Bank expects Dayang's topside maintenance services order-book conversion to rise to 16 per cent in FY27 and marine charter utilisation to improve to 74 per cent.
"While delayed approvals and work orders from the operational transition continue to weigh on activity, the transfer of Carigali assets to Vestigo should improve activity visibility once funding arrangements among the PACs are resolved," it said.
The firm said a resolution between Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) and Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) is nearing, with the Carigali-Vestigo transition providing a positive signal that delayed activity could resume.
The firm maintained its "Buy" call on the stock with a lower target price of RM2.
Meanwhile, Phillip Capital expects Dayang's earnings to remain flat in the third quarter as subdued topside maintenance services continue to weigh on its maintenance, construction and modification contributions amid the prolonged Petronas-Petros resolution.
The softer maintenance outlook should, however, be partly offset by stronger contributions from marine charter.
"Perdana Petroleum is expected to mobilise an additional accommodation work barge, lifting utilisation, while its AHTS fleet continues to operate at a healthy 80 per cent utilisation.
"Dayang's own work barges also remain fully deployed under long-term contracts. Overall, we expect the stronger marine charter contribution to provide a near-term earnings cushion against softer maintenance activity," it said in a note.
Phillip Capital maintained its "Hold" call on the stock with a target price of RM1.60.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High Court slashes man’s rape sentence from 10 years to one, citing youth and rehabilitation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — The High Court in Kuantan has slashed a man’s sentence for statutory rape from 10 years’ imprisonment and six strokes of the cane to one year’s jail and two strokes.
In allowing the 23-year-old’s appeal against the penalty, Judicial Commissioner Samry Masri ruled that the Sessions Court had failed to give adequate weight to the accused’s youth, his clean record as a first offender, and his strong prospects for rehabilitation,
FMT
reported.
The accused was 19 years old when he committed the offences on October 8 and October 29, 2022. At the time, he worked in the dining hall of a residential school in Kuantan where the 15-year-old complainant, identified in court documents as SP4, was a student.
He was initially convicted after trial on two counts of rape under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code. The Sessions Court had handed down five years’ imprisonment and three strokes of the rotan for each charge, ordering the sentences to run consecutively.
Samry upheld the underlying convictions, affirming that because of the complainant’s age, consent remained legally irrelevant under Section 375(g) of the Penal Code.
However, the judicial commissioner held that sentencing must remain nuanced and tailored to individual circumstances.
“The appellant’s prospects of rehabilitation also remain relevant. He was a young first offender and the evidence did not show a continuing predatory risk requiring a lengthy period of incapacitation,” Samry said in his 40-page written judgment.
Samry noted that the circumstances were “materially different from sexual offending involving predation, grooming, coercion or exploitation”.
In mitigating the penalty, the judge took into account the pre-existing relationship between the parties, the victim’s proximity to the age of 16, the manner in which their meetings were coordinated, and the absence of systemic grooming or calculated exploitation.
Under the revised sentence, the appellant will serve six months’ jail and receive one stroke for the first charge, and one year’s jail with one stroke for the second charge. The custodial sentences will run concurrently, meaning he will serve a total of one year behind bars.
The High Court maintained accompanying orders requiring the man to undergo rehabilitative counselling alongside two years of post-release police supervision.
Samry emphasised that the reduced sentence should not be misconstrued as recognising a minor’s agreement as a defence against statutory rape, stressing that judicial penalties must remain “just, proportionate and responsive to the circumstances of each offence”.

Title: Police: Plantation supervisor seriously injured in machete attack at workers’ quarters in Gua Musang
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 25 — A plantation supervisor was seriously injured after being attacked by a group of individuals armed with machetes, iron rods and wooden clubs during an altercation at a workers’ quarters in Kampung RKT Kesedar Chalil, Gua Musang, yesterday.
Gua Musang police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said the incident occurred at about 3.15pm after a group of men, believed to be representatives of a company with interests in the area, arrived at the quarters to seek clarification regarding permits to enter a forest reserve.
“A dispute broke out when a man was allegedly assaulted by two individuals from the group. A plantation worker who attempted to intervene was subsequently attacked by the group using weapons such as machetes, iron rods and wooden clubs,” he said in a statement today.
He said the 35-year-old local man sustained several serious injuries, including a fractured left arm and shinbone, an injured tendon in his left leg, bruising and swelling around his left eye, as well as a nosebleed.
Sik said the case was being investigated under Sections 326 and 148 of the Penal Code.
“The police advise the public against making any speculation regarding the incident that could cause confusion within the community,” he said.
Members of the public with information are urged to contact the nearest police station or Paloh Police Station at 09-928 5090. — Bernama

Title: Zahid backs PAC move to probe Tabung Haji management since 2017, stresses facts over perception
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi supports a proposal for the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) to establish a special body to investigate the management of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2017 to the present.
Ahmad Zahid said the investigation was important to clarify what had happened after 2017 based on facts and reality, while also helping to correct public perceptions regarding TH’s management and governance.
He said the proposal was informally put forward by several Members of Parliament who attended the “Reality and Perception: Don’t Politicise Tabung Haji” forum held in conjunction with the Musyawarah Nasional, which aimed to examine and clarify aspects of TH’s governance and management, particularly matters raised in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH covering the period from 2014 to 2020.
“In my view, this is a recommendation that should be followed so that there are no accusations of ‘embezzlement’, while the certificate issued by the National Audit Department (JAN), which clearly shows that a clean certificate was issued, indicates that the audit conducted on TH was based on its governing Act. The Tabung Haji Act 1995 states that the National Audit Department is responsible for auditing it.
“This is what the PAC should look into so that the facts can correct public perceptions and reflect the reality that the public wants to know,” he told reporters after attending the forum here today.
Asked whether the proposal to establish the special body would be brought to the Cabinet, Ahmad Zahid said this was unnecessary as the PAC has the appropriate mandate and responsibility to conduct the investigation.
“I do not think it needs to be brought to the Cabinet because this forum was for clarification, and in my view, what was informally proposed earlier by the MPs should be given priority.
“Especially for the PAC to establish an investigative body under the PAC’s own responsibility. This would be more appropriate than other approaches,” he said.
Asked about the proposal to establish a new RCI to investigate TH’s management from 2017 to the present, Ahmad Zahid said the PAC would be more suitable to conduct the investigation as it has clear jurisdiction to do so.
“I think the PAC is more suitable to conduct the investigation because it has the locus standi, as set out in the PAC’s own duties and responsibilities,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s SMART rescue team prepares for United Nations reclassification, aims to retain status
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — The Malaysian Special Search and Rescue Team (SMART) is determined to retain its Heavy Urban Search and Rescue (Heavy USAR) classification under the United Nations (UN) as a special “gift” to Malaysia in conjunction with the 69th National Day celebrations.
SMART Team Commander PgKB I Abdul Manaf Che Isa said the country’s elite rescue team is scheduled to undergo the INSARAG External Reclassification (IER) assessment from Sept 20 to 24 to retain the classification, which it first obtained in 2016.
The official reassessment process will be conducted after confirmation from the INSARAG Secretariat in Geneva, Switzerland, while the team’s final technical preparations will begin on Sept 20.
Abdul Manaf expressed confidence in SMART’s level of preparedness after undergoing three large-scale pre-IER exercises, including one simulation last year and two this year.
“We are very confident because the mentor we appointed from Australia was very satisfied with the three large-scale exercises we conducted.
“We are ready to face the IER in September, and this will be a gift to the nation for this year’s National Day celebrations. Hopefully, we will succeed,” he told Bernama recently.
Abdul Manaf explained that Malaysia was the second country in Asia after Singapore to receive the prestigious classification from the International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) in 2016.
He said the classification must be renewed every five years to ensure that the team’s capabilities and expertise continue to comply with international standards. However, the process had previously been rescheduled due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
He said retaining the Heavy USAR status was crucial as it serves as recognition of SMART’s level of expertise, while also enabling the team to remain a key reference for countries in the Asian region in search and rescue operations and disaster management.
“Our expertise serves as a reference for countries in the Asian region in conducting operations and managing disasters in an orderly and systematic manner according to international norms and standards,” he said.
Abdul Manaf said the classification also enables SMART to be deployed as part of the international disaster assistance framework under the UN, demonstrating the country’s capabilities on par with other global rescue teams.
Among the key criteria for a Heavy USAR team is the ability to operate independently (self-sufficient) when deployed to disaster zones, including managing logistics, food supplies and communication systems, as well as establishing a base of operations without placing a burden on the affected country.
“It is not merely about saving lives and property; we are capable of operating without any assistance. That is what is very important about this classification for a country,” he said.
On its participation in the National Day celebrations on Aug 31, he said about 100 SMART members and personnel would take part in the parade at Dataran Putrajaya to showcase their readiness to the public.
The participation will also include an exhibition of the team’s strategic assets, comprising two heavy vehicles and four Utility Terrain Vehicles (UTVs).
The 2026 National Day celebrations will be held at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31, with the theme
Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati
. — Bernama

Title: Lee Lam Thye urges urgent review of Asean haze pact, calls for enforceable action plan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Asean leaders have been urged to conduct an urgent high-level review of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution and adopt a stronger, time-bound and enforceable regional action plan to prevent the haze situation from worsening.
Social activist Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye said the recurring transboundary haze crisis could no longer be treated as a seasonal inconvenience, saying that Asean must move from reaction to prevention and strengthen regional preparedness.
He said the agreement, signed in Kuala Lumpur on June 10, 2002 and came into force in 2003, had been in place for more than two decades, yet the region continued to grapple with recurring fires, cross-border smoke and deteriorating air quality.
“We must stop treating haze as an annual Asean ritual. Haze is not merely a weather problem. It is a governance, environmental, public health and regional responsibility problem.
“After more than 20 years, Asean must move beyond promises and demonstrate that regional cooperation can actually protect the people of Southeast Asia,” he said in a statement today.
Lee said the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre had warned that strengthening El Niño conditions, below-normal rainfall and prevailing winds could increase the risk of hotspots and transboundary haze in the southern Asean region.
However, he said El Niño should not be used as the sole explanation for the problem, as it is a natural climate phenomenon, while human-caused forest and land fires continue to turn dry conditions into a regional crisis.
Among the urgent measures he proposed were strengthening and reviewing the implementation of the regional haze agreement, including setting clear, measurable targets to prevent fires, reduce hotspots, and eliminate recurring sources of transboundary pollution.
He also called for stronger accountability for companies or individuals responsible for open burning and illegal land clearing, as well as mechanisms for investigation, evidence-sharing and enforcement when fires cause cross-border damage.
At the same time, Lee proposed a permanent regional haze response mechanism involving real-time satellite monitoring, rapid sharing of hotspot information, joint firefighting capabilities and clearly defined responsibilities during serious haze episodes.
He said Asean countries should also establish joint prevention and early-warning systems ahead of the dry season, strengthen cooperation on peatland and forest management, and improve transparency in sharing information on hotspots, fire sources and enforcement action.
Malaysia and other affected countries, he said, should be prepared to raise the issue firmly at the highest level of Asean, stressing that tackling the problem was not about blaming or interfering in the affairs of any country but about ensuring the health and well-being of all. — Bernama

Title: Man arrested in Chow Kit hotel over Quran burning, theft investigations
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 25 — Police arrested a man at a hotel in Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur, yesterday to assist investigations into the burning and theft of copies of the Quran.
Negeri Sembilan Police Chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the 25-year-old suspect was arrested following a public complaint about a fire near a field in Senawang on Aug 22.
“Investigations revealed that the fire involved several copies of the Quran. Police later received a report at about 4.45pm the same day regarding the theft of copies from a mosque in Forest Heights here.
“The suspect was subsequently arrested at about 9.30pm last night during a raid at a hotel in Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur,” he said in a statement here today.
He said police found two bags containing 16 copies of the Quran during a search of the hotel room and seized three mobile phones as well as the suspect’s personal belongings.
Alzafny said all the copies of the Quran recovered from the suspect were believed to have been taken without permission from mosques and surau in the Chow Kit area.
“We are not ruling out the possibility that some of the copies were taken from a university in the north, following the discovery of the university’s ownership stamp.
“A search was also conducted at the suspect’s family home in Senawang on the same day, resulting in the seizure of 36 Quran covers from his room,” he said.
Alzafny said initial investigations found a link between the discovery and the Quran-burning incident on Aug 22, with the case being investigated under Sections 380 and 295 of the Penal Code.
He said checks revealed that the suspect had four previous criminal records and had just completed a two-month police supervision order. — Bernama

Title: Hot weather and strong winds complicate firefighting as 51‑hectare Kota Tinggi peat blaze rages
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Aug 25 — Hot weather and strong winds are complicating efforts to put out a 51.4-hectare peat fire along Jalan Bypass Sebana Cove-Punggai that started yesterday.
Operations commander, Deputy Fire Supt II Baharuddin Idris said 9.7 per cent of the fire in Sector A, which is 35.6 hectares, and the entire area of Sektor B (15.8 hectares), was under control
“Our main challenges are strong winds, hot weather and limited water supply. We get water by using water tankers with the help of related agencies, including Ranhill SAJ.
“No new fires have been detected in the area, and there have been no casualties reported due to the fire,” he said when met by reporters at the site of the fire here today.
He explained that they were using the direct attack method while waiting for two excavators from other agencies scheduled to arrive at noon as the department needed larger amphibious excavators that are capable of operating in peat and forest areas to create firebreaks, especially in Sector A.
Baharuddin said there was a risk that the fire could spread if winds got stronger, but the situation in Sector B was under control.
“We hope if the weather isn’t too hot, we can put out the fire there (Sector B). But in Sector A, we still need help to create firebreaks using amphibious excavators,” he said.
The fire was not threatening residential areas as the nearest housing area was in Sebana Cove almost three kilometres away, while Punggal was about four to five kilometres from the fire, while the road has been closed to the public since 2pm yesterday.
Fire and Rescue Department personnel battling the blaze along the Punggai–Sebana Cove bypass. — Bernama pic
The area on fire is categorised as agriculture land, with a small part of the nearby area being an oil palm plantation owned by Keledang Felda while other areas have yet to be cultivated, he added.
The cause of the fire has yet to be determined, Baharuddin said, and investigations are ongoing.
“There are people who enter this area, probably to fish, but we cannot determine if it has any relation to the cause of the fire,” he said, adding that 21 personnel, including four Civil Defence Force members were involved in firefighting efforts.
Meanwhile, Tanjung Surat assemblyman Aznan Tamin advised local residents to follow the instructions of the authorties and to avoid using the closed Punggal bypass and to use alternative routes.
He also advised that nearby residents, especially those in Taman Bayu Damai and Punggai, to wear facemasks if they are exposed to thick smoke as the Air Pollution Index (API) reading in the area has risen slightly to 125.
