“In light of this incident, I hope everyone will be more cautious and not conduct open burning, especially during hot weather,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Thousands join Maulidur Rasul nationwide, Anwar leads UPM procession under Madani Dihayati theme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Thousands of Muslims nationwide today joined Maulidur Rasul 1448H/2026M celebrations through processions and selawat recitations, commemorating the life and teachings of Prophet Muhammad SAW.
Held under the theme
Madani Dihayati, Ummah Diberkati
, this year’s celebrations brought together Muslims from all walks of life, as well as government agencies, the private sector and non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
At the national level, the celebration at Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM), Serdang was attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, with more than 4,000 people, including procession contingents.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) director-general Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee.
In his speech, Anwar said appreciation of Islam should not stop at Maulidur Rasul celebrations or processions, but should instead be reflected through the appreciation of Prophet Muhammad SAW’s life and teachings as a blessing to all mankind.
He said the celebration should serve as a platform to instil spirit, awareness and enlightenment among Muslims.
In SELANGOR, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah graced the state-level Maulidur Rasul Celebration at the Shah Alam Islamic Lecture and Muzakarah Hall.
Also present were Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin, Selangor Islamic Religious Council chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin and State Islamic Religion and Cultural Innovation Committee chairman Dr Mohamad Fahmi Ngah.
The event was attended by nearly 1,000 participants, with Sultan Sharafuddin also presenting the Maulidur Rasul Figure Award to Hindon Abdullah, 84, a prominent figure in the Muslim women’s dakwah movement and in family and community development in Selangor.
In NEGERI SEMBILAN, Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, accompanied by their son, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin, graced the state-level celebration at the Royale Chulan Hotel Hall.
Also present were Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid.
However, the procession involving 4,000 participants from 74 contingents comprising government and private agencies, public higher education institutions, students and persons with disabilities (PwD) was halted due to continuous heavy rain.
Heavy rain drenches the Seremban City Council field, the main venue for Negeri Sembilan’s Maulidur Rasul procession today. — Bernama pic
In JOHOR, Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi led a procession involving 5,000 participants in conjunction with the state-level Maulidur Rasul celebration in Batu Pahat.
A total of 50 contingents marched one kilometre from the Batu Pahat District Office compound to the Sultan Ismail Mosque, with the Johor Bahru City Council, which sent 200 participants, emerging as the contingent with the largest participation.
Also taking part in the procession were State Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khali, Johor State Mufti Datuk Yahya Ahmad and members of the state government committee.
In TERENGGANU, the Regent of Terengganu Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, graced the Maulidur Rasul celebration, which was also attended by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar and State Information, Dakwah and Syariah Empowerment Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Khalil Abdul Hadi.
At the event, attended by about 1,000 guests, he also presented the Ummah Volunteer Award to community organisation Gong Tok Nasek Care and International Humanitarian Flotilla Mission activist Muhd Asmawi Mukhtar @ Awang.
The Islamic Author Award was presented to Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA) Faculty of Islamic Contemporary Studies lecturer Prof Dr Engku Ahmad Zaki Engku Alwi.
Participants at Terengganu’s state‑level Maulidur Rasul celebration at Stadium Negeri. — Bernama pic
In KEDAH, the Sultan of Kedah Al Aminul Karim Sultan Sallehuddin Sultan Badlishah, graced the state-level Maulidur Rasul celebration at Wisma Darulaman alongside the Raja Muda of Kedah, Tengku Sarafudin Badlishah Sultan Sallehuddin.
The event, attended by more than 500 people, featured Quranic recitation, a royal address by Sultan Sallehuddin, a special Maulidur Rasul video screening and a Marhaban performance.
His Royal Highness also presented the Imam Figure Award to the Imama of Jame’ As-Shahab Kepala Batas Mosque Che Ismail Bakar, while former Kedah Mufti Datuk Paduka Syeikh Hasbullah Abdul Halim received the state-level Special Award.
Meanwhile in PERAK, the Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah and the Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, graced the state-level Maulidur Rasul Celebration at the Casuarina Convention Centre in Ipoh.
Also present were the Raja Muda of Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and the Raja Di Hilir of Perak Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah, as well as Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and his wife, Datin Seri Aezer Zubin.
About 2,000 attendees enlivened the event, which was graced with the recitation of the Asmaul Husna, the reading of holy verses from the Quran and mass selawat.
Sultan Nazrin also consented to presenting awards to several Maulidur Rasul figures this year, among them veteran director and actor Datuk Rahim Razali, who received the Zaid Bin Thabit Award (Communications and Media Practitioner).
In MELAKA, Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam led the Maulidur Rasul procession involving nearly 7,000 participants from 101 contingents, starting from the Tun Fatimah Stadium in Bukit Serindit to the Islamic Centre Square in Bukit Baru.
The procession was also joined by Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, as well as State Housing, Local Government, Drainage, Climate Change and Disaster Management Committee chairman Datuk Rais Yasin and State Education, Higher Education and Religious Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Rahmad Mariman.
In PENANG, Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Ramli Ngah Talib and his wife Toh Puan Raja Noora Ashikin Raja Abdullah attended the state-level Maulidur Rasul celebration at the Seberang Perai Selatan District Mosque, accompanied by Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Dr Mohamad Abdul Hamid.
Former Penang State Secretary Datuk Seri Zulkifli Long was crowned the state-level Maulidur Rasul Figure this year.
Also receiving awards were RCAB Food Venture Sdn Bhd managing director Rohaya Che Abu Bakar for the Qudwatur Rasul (Entrepreneur) award, Kuala Lumpur High Court Judicial Commissioner Datuk Muhammad Adam Abdullah for the Qudwatur Rasul (Saudara Kita) award and Penang State Mufti Department Chief Officer (Researcher) Mohd Salmi Shaimi for the Qudwatur Rasul (Special) award.
Earlier, a total of 44 contingents with 1,320 participants from government agencies, uniformed bodies, and NGOs joined a 300-metre procession starting from Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Jawi to the Seberang Perai Selatan District Mosque.
In PAHANG, the Regent of Pahang Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah graced the state-level Maulidur Rasul celebration at the Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Convention Centre in Pekan.
Former Pahang State Financial Officer Datuk Norzan Ahmad was crowned the 2026/1448 Hijrah Pahang Maulidur Rasul Figure, taking home a certificate of appreciation, a plaque and a cash prize of RM10,000.
Also present were State Islamic Religious Affairs, Rural Development and Orang Asli Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Syed Ahmad, Pahang State Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Seri Mohd Sharkar Shamsudin, State Secretary Datuk Seri Nazri Abu Bakar and Pahang Islamic Religious Department director Datuk Ahmad Khirrizal Ab Rahman.
In SABAH, Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Musa Aman officiated the state-level Maulidur Rasul Celebration, which took place at the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) in Kota Kinabalu.
Also present were his wife Toh Puan Faridah Tussin, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, Sabah State Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Seri Kadzim M Yahya, Deputy Chief Minister II Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun and Sabah Local Government and Housing Minister Datuk Dr Mohd Arifin Mohd Arif, who is also the main celebration committee chairman.
Over 10,000 attendees enlivened the event, having previously marched in 96 contingents from Padang Merdeka to the SICC.
Kampung Seri Pulau residents parade with Jalur Gemilang on horseback during Maulidur Rasul and National Month celebrations in Kubang Kerian. — Bernama pic
In KELANTAN, the Maulidur Rasul and National Month celebrations at the Al Taqwa Mosque in Kubang Kerian were also enlivened by the participation of over 20 horses and 400 participants.
Seri Pulau Rukun Tetangga Area (KRT) chairman Mat Zohari Abdullah said the participation of horses in the procession was sparked by the suggestion of a local horse breeder who wanted to contribute to the success of the programme.
He noted that the presence of the horses also holds symbolic value, as the animals were among the mounts used since the time of Prophet Muhammad SAW, in addition to serving various functions in the lives of past societies. — Bernama

Title: Malaysians advised to reconsider non‑essential travel to Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat amid unrest
Article:
KANGAR, Aug 25 — Malaysians in Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat, as well as those planning to travel there, have been urged to remain vigilant following a series of recent security incidents in the three southern Thai provinces.
Malaysia’s Consul General in Songkhla, Thailand, Ahmad Fahmi Ahmad Sarkawi, said those planning to travel to the affected areas were advised to reconsider non-essential travel.
“Malaysians are also advised to avoid areas affected by security incidents, demonstrations or large gatherings and to comply with instructions from the Thai authorities, including those on curfews, road closures and security checks,” he said in a statement from Istana Arau today.
Media previously reported that Narathiwat was placed under a curfew from 10.15pm on Aug 22 to 5am on Aug 23, following more than 50 incidents, including bombings and the burning of local government offices and tyres in the three provinces.
Ahmad Fahmi made the remarks while attending the Kayuhan Malaysia Merdeka 2026 programme around the Ko Taeo subdistrict in Songkhla, led by the Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail and the second heir to the Perlis throne, Syed Sirajuddin Areeb Putra Al-Haj Jamalullail.
Ahmad Fahmi also urged Malaysians to avoid travelling at night in affected areas, follow official announcements and keep their immediate family members informed of their travel plans.
Meanwhile, he advised Malaysians driving into Thailand to carry their original physical driving licence and not rely solely on the digital licence available through the MyJPJ application.
“Important documents, including vehicle registration, insurance and other required documents, should be carried throughout the journey to facilitate checks by the authorities
“Malaysians driving or riding in Thailand are also reminded to wear seat belts or helmets at all times and comply with all traffic regulations enforced by the Thai authorities,” he said.
Ahmad Fahmi said the Thai authorities are now actively enforcing traffic regulations, including on Malaysian-registered vehicles, with several Malaysian drivers reportedly issued summonses for documentation and traffic-related offences. — Bernama

Title: Prime Minister urges Muslims to reflect Prophet’s values, not limit Maulidur Rasul to celebrations
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the commemoration of Maulidur Rasul should not be limited to celebrations or processions, but should instead be reflected through practising Prophet Muhammad’s (PBUH) way of life as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity.
He said the Maulidur Rasul celebration should serve as a platform to inspire Muslims with renewed spirit, awareness and enlightenment.
“In the context of understanding Islam, the challenge lies in its practice and how we perceive it. Like the month of independence, it is not about the celebration, festivities or procession, but what matters most is upholding the commands of Allah SWT,” he said.
“For me, this celebration is meant to inspire a renewed spirit, not to perpetuate old complacency. The torch of Islam remains dynamic and alive. Every episode in the life of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) offers a lesson for us,” he said in his speech at the national-level Maulidur Rasul 1448/2026 celebration here today.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, and Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) director-general Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee.
Anwar said the challenge for Muslims today is to internalise Islamic values and become a role model not only for fellow Muslims, but also for all Malaysians and the global community.
He said the concept of
rahmatan lil ‘alamin
(mercy to all creation) must be translated into building a society rooted in values, principles and ideals, while driven by the pursuit of excellence.
Anwar said a society built on the principles taught by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) must uphold clear values, including embracing goodness, respecting others and upholding justice, while rejecting wrongdoing, social ills, arrogance, narrow-minded racism, oppression, corruption and abuse of power.
“How can we build the Malay and Muslim communities in Malaysia based on the principles taught by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) into a distinguished, unique and exceptional society that moves towards excellence?
“This is the test and challenge as we commemorate the birth of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). The occasion should not be limited to celebrations, processions or ceremonies, but must inspire deeper reflection and understanding. This is what I mean by an ecumenical community par excellence,” he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the current approach to
dakwah
(Islamic outreach) required attention, particularly in ensuring that the delivery of religious messages encouraged understanding and acceptance.
“When we look at our Islamic outreach efforts today, some people are becoming less receptive to Islam. This is unlike the example demonstrated by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), whom we recognise as the finest example.
“This is a reminder to all of us. How can we improve?” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore reaffirm commitment to free and safe Strait of Malacca
Article:
SINGAPORE, Aug 25 — Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore reaffirmed their shared commitment to keep the Strait of Malacca and Singapore Strait free, open and safe for international shipping.
The commitment was made by the Malaysia Marine Department, Indonesia’s Directorate General of Sea Transportation, and the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) in a joint statement issued during 17th Co-operation Forum on Tuesday.
They underscored the importance of respecting navigational rights and freedoms both in principle and in practice, affirming the waterways are “Strait Used for International Navigation”, where the right of transit passage applies under the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and customary international law.
Meanwhile, Singapore Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow said the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (SOMS) are a primary artery for global trade, with more than 100,000 vessels passing through the waterways each year.
They carry almost a quarter of global seaborne trade and almost a third of the world’s oil and gas supplies.
“Events in the West Asia this year reminded the world that open sea lanes can never be taken for granted.
“In our part of the world, we will endeavour to keep the Straits of Malacca and Singapore free, open and safe for international shipping,” he said during the opening of the forum.
Siow noted that the Cooperative Mechanism, formalised in 2007, stands as the first and only implementation of Article 43 of UNCLOS which calls on countries to cooperate on navigational safety and pollution prevention.
Through the Cooperative Mechanism, countries have turned shared interests into collective action in three key areas: anticipating risks early, regularly upgrading infrastructure, and responding collectively to incidents. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Amirudin tasked to work out Pakatan-BN alliance details for Melaka polls
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 25 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has been given the mandate to work out the details of proposed cooperation between the coalition and Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka state election, said PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, who is also the prime minister, said Amirudin had been entrusted with looking into the matter.
“We have given Amir (Amirudin) the responsibility to work it out,” he told the media after attending the National Maulidur Rasul Celebration 1448/2026 here today.
He was responding to a question about reports that his meeting with Amirudin, who is also the Selangor Menteri Besar, had also discussed seat allocations for the Melaka election.
However, Anwar clarified that the meeting was related to the Malaysia Games (Sukma), not politics.
“I met the Selangor menteri besar regarding Sukma. During the Games, when would there be time for politics?” he said.
Asked about the possibility of cooperation between political parties in the Melaka polls, Anwar said cooperation was important in life and administration.
“Room for cooperation... in life, we must cooperate. This is all about cooperation,” he said before leaving.
Yesterday, PH communications director and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil confirmed that Amirudin had met Anwar the previous day.
Anwar was previously reported to have said that the PH election committee would discuss the possibility of cooperation with BN for the Melaka election.
He said the committee is led by Amirudin and PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. — Bernama

Title: Sultan Nazrin calls for less political rivalry among Malaysia’s Muslim leaders
Article:
IPOH, Aug 25 — The unity of Muslims is facing growing challenges due to differences in politics, religious schools of thought, race and personal interests, Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah said.
Sultan Nazrin said these factors, coupled with the pursuit of influence, rank, position, wealth and worldly comforts, were increasingly overshadowing the spirit of brotherhood, causing ukhuwah among Muslims to be sidelined.
He stressed that Muslim leaders, Islamic organisations and movements should avoid unnecessary disputes and minimise political rivalry, while giving greater priority to initiatives that could strengthen the identity and progress of the ummah.
“It is encouraging and something for which we should be grateful that while political leaders and groups choose to compete and engage in disputes, there are also individuals and organisations pioneering positive efforts to raise awareness in Islamic education.
“These include Islamic economics, Islamic finance, the halal industry, waqf, digital dakwah and strengthening family institutions. Such efforts must be expanded, reinforced and successfully implemented,” Sultan Nazrin said in his royal address at the Perak-level Maulidur Rasul celebration here today.
Also present were the Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Perak Raja Muda Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and Raja Di Hilir Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah.
Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and his wife Datin Seri Aezer Zubin were also in attendance.
The Sultan also highlighted the challenges facing Muslim identity and the values of the ummah due to increasing exposure to global influences, including social media, popular culture, entertainment and modern lifestyles.
He said wise approaches and strategies were needed to ensure that progress and modernisation did not erode Islamic principles and identity.
“Efforts must be made to strike a balance so that modernisation does not lead to a loss of confidence in one’s own identity,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Prime Minister confirms Felda forensic audit proposal will be tabled at Cabinet meeting soon
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 25 — A proposal for a forensic audit to be conducted into the management of the Federal Land Consolidation and Rehabilitation Authority (Felda) will be discussed by the Cabinet, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“We will bring it to the Cabinet meeting for discussion,” he told the media briefly after attending the National Maulidur Rasul Celebration at Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) here today.
Anwar was responding to a question about Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s suggestion that a forensic audit be conducted to determine whether there had been abuse of power, breach of trust or governance violations in Felda’s management.
On Aug 23, Ahmad Zahid said a management audit alone was insufficient, given that issues involving the agency had persisted for a long time and resulted in losses amounting to billions of ringgit.
Previously, Anwar said he would await the full report by the special task force investigating Felda’s management issues before making any official announcement.
He said the task force had begun its work and its findings were expected to be presented soon before being made public, similar to the report by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Tabung Haji. — Bernama

Title: Haze alert: Penang health exco advises face masks as API levels spike
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 25 — Residents of Penang are urged to limit outdoor activities as air quality deteriorated today, with three of the state's four monitoring stations breaching the unhealthy threshold.
State youth, sports and health committee chairman Daniel Gooi advised the public to wear face masks when outdoors to mitigate the effects of the poor air quality.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), readings as of 11am showed unhealthy levels across most of the state.
On the island, the Minden and Balik Pulau stations recorded APIs of 155 and 151 respectively, while the Seberang Perai station on the mainland logged a reading of 146.
The only station remaining in the moderate category was Seberang Jaya, which recorded an API of 96.
Gooi urged the public to strictly adhere to the health ministry's guidelines during this period. These protocols include reducing prolonged outdoor exposure, wearing face masks, and minimizing indoor air pollution, such as avoiding smoking.
The public is also advised to stay hydrated, wash their hands and face after being outdoors, and utilize the internal air circulation mode when using vehicle air conditioners.
Addressing the medical impact of the haze, Gooi noted that the state is on standby for an increase in health complications.
“So far there have not been report of acute respiratory cases due to the haze, but State Health Department have prepared for this,” he said.
He added that anyone experiencing respiratory distress should seek immediate treatment at public healthcare facilities.

Title: Immigration lodges police report after viral UTC Pudu post found inconsistent with CCTV records
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — The Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM) has lodged a police report over a viral post concerning an applicant’s experience at the UTC Pudu Sentral Immigration Branch Office.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said a review found that several allegations in the post were inconsistent with closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, related records and statements from officers on duty at the time of the incident.
In a statement today, he said the review was conducted by examining CCTV footage and related records, as well as obtaining statements from the officers involved.
“The department takes this matter seriously to ensure the actual situation can be clarified based on the facts obtained. A police report has been lodged and JIM will provide its full cooperation to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM),” he said.
Zakaria said JIM respected the right of every individual to voice their views, share their experiences or submit complaints regarding the department’s services.
However, he stressed that accurate and comprehensive information was important to ensure matters could be evaluated fairly and to avoid misunderstandings.
He said JIM remained committed to handling every complaint transparently, professionally and without prejudice, while continuing to provide courteous services with integrity and prioritising the interests of the public. — Bernama

Title: MACC probes RM80m Felda Palong 7 oil palm replanting scheme after settlers raise concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is examining information related to the implementation of the oil palm development and replanting programme at Felda Palong 7 in Wilayah Raja Alias, Bandar Sri Jempol, Negeri Sembilan, including concerns over the quality of the seedlings supplied and their compliance with the required specifications.
In a statement, MACC said the information was received from Pertubuhan Badan Bertindak Generasi Palong (Perbagi) chairman Mohd Syahrizal Md Yusuf, who raised concerns over the quality of the oil palm seedlings and the implementation of the programme.
The commission said the matters raised included the supply, delivery, storage and age of the oil palm seedlings, as well as whether they complied with the required specifications.
“MACC has taken note of the allegations and concerns raised and will examine the information to determine whether they involve any offences under its jurisdiction,” the statement said.
MACC said it also took note of the request for the relevant technical agency to conduct an inspection of the seedlings, particularly in terms of their quality and compliance with the stipulated specifications.
“Any further action will be determined based on the findings of the investigation and information obtained,” the statement said.
The oil palm replanting programme is reported to benefit about 450 settlers in the area.
MACC stressed that receiving the information did not mean that any party had committed an offence and should not be regarded as a conclusion against any individual or party involved.
Media previously reported that a group of new-generation Felda Palong 7 settlers had urged MACC to investigate the implementation of the oil palm development and replanting programme, which involves an estimated RM70 million to RM80 million. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds across four states and Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Four states in Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak are expected to experience thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds until 1 pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the whole of Perlis and Melaka are expected to be affected.
In Kedah, the warning covers Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Pokok Sena and Padang Terap.
In Selangor, the areas forecast to be hit are Kuala Selangor, Sabak Bernam, Hulu Selangor and Gombak, while in Sarawak, the areas involved are Bintulu and several areas in Miri, namely Subis, Miri, Beluru and Marudi.
Meanwhile, in a separate statement, MetMalaysia also issued a Tropical Storm Advisory (NARRA) after a tropical storm was detected in northwestern China today, but stressed that the phenomenon would not have a significant impact on Malaysia.
According to MetMalaysia, the tropical storm was detected at latitude 19.9° north and longitude 108.0° east, about 114 kilometres northwest of Basuo, China, and 1,650 km north of Tumpat, Kelantan, as of 8 am today, with maximum wind speeds of 65 kph. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak and Klang Valley worst hit as 30 spots in Malaysia breach ‘Unhealthy’ API levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Malaysia’s prolonged haze crisis showed no signs of abating today, with 30 monitoring stations nationwide recording “unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels, according to data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
An API reading between 101 and 200 is categorised as unhealthy, posing potential health risks to the general public while placing vulnerable groups, including young children, the elderly, and individuals with chronic respiratory illnesses, at heightened risk.
Sarawak remained the epicentre of the country's worst air pollution. The IPD Serian monitoring station recorded the highest reading nationwide at 180, inching toward the “very unhealthy” threshold of 201. Sri Aman trailed closely at 169, while Samarahan and Sarikei registered 157 and 152 respectively.
Authorities have tied Sarawak's deteriorating air quality to a convergence of transboundary smoke, dry weather intensified by the El Niño phenomenon, and localized peat and forest fires.
Across the peninsula, the Klang Valley was smothered by a blanket of acrid smog, with half a dozen stations across Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, and Putrajaya crossing into the unhealthy tier.
Shah Alam recorded the highest reading in Peninsular Malaysia and the third highest nationwide at 162. Putrajaya posted 156, followed by Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur and Kuala Selangor at 155 each, Banting at 152, and Petaling Jaya at 151.
Air quality deteriorated significantly across other peninsular states as well. Perak logged widespread unhealthy air, led by Tanjung Malim, Seri Manjung, Tasek Ipoh, and Taiping with readings ranging between 152 and 155, while Pengkalan in Ipoh stood at 137.
In Johor, Segamat, Batu Pahat, and Tangkak all reached 152, while Kota Tinggi recorded 119. Elsewhere, Nilai in Negeri Sembilan and Bukit Rambai in Melaka tied at 155, Alor Gajah registered 151, while both Sungai Petani in Kedah and Balik Pulau in Penang logged 152.
The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability reiterated that this month's widespread haze stems from prolonged dry spells linked to El Niño, below-average rainfall, and extensive domestic and cross-border open burning.
Members of the public, particularly high-risk individuals such as expectant mothers, senior citizens, and patients with cardiac or pulmonary conditions, are advised to minimise outdoor exposure, wear protective face masks, maintain high hydration levels, and strictly refrain from open burning.

Title: Civil Defence Force vows safety review after trained sergeant dies from cobra bite
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The Malaysia Civil Defence Force (APM) takes the fatal snakebite incident involving one of its personnel seriously and remains open to reviewing and improving safety measures, risk management and the implementation of activities from time to time.
It said that this is following the tragedy that claimed the life of Sergeant (PA) Muhamad Muazam Shah Kamardin after he completed his participation in the Public Awareness Training Programme on the Handling of Venomous Animals at the Taman Temerloh Jaya Hall, Pahang, on Saturday (Aug 22).
“The assessment measures are part of APM’s ongoing commitment to ensuring the safety and welfare of its personnel remain a priority,” it said in a statement today.
APM also confirmed that the 39-year-old was a trained personnel, with extensive experience in handling venomous animals and had been actively serving since 2010.
“APM stresses that the venomous animal handling activity was carried out in accordance with the stipulated standard operating procedures (SOPs) and safety procedures.
“All APM personnel are required to undergo relevant training before being allowed to participate in operations, and the personnel involved also carried out their duties based on the stipulated procedures and safety instructions,” it added.
Muhamad Muazam Shah, who was bitten on the finger of his right hand by a king cobra during a demonstration, was confirmed to have died at 1.50am Sunday while receiving treatment at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (HoSHAS) in Temerloh.
APM also expressed its condolences to the deceased’s family, describing his passing as a major loss to APM and the country. — Bernama

Title: Anwar reflects on Prophet’s leadership, promises change and justice for Malaysia in Maulidur Rasul message
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that he will continue striving to bring about change and reform (
islah
) for the country, taking the strategy of Prophet Muhammad SAW in establishing a new administration in the Arab region over 14 centuries ago as a reference.
In a Facebook post yesterday in conjunction with today’s Maulidur Rasul celebration, Anwar said it is not easy to develop a pluralistic nation in South-east Asia in the 21st century with all its political crises and complexities, but he will continue striving to do his best for Malaysia.
“Basic needs must be guaranteed, and tangible peace is of the utmost importance. This resolve is a prerequisite for ensuring the essentials (daruriyat) in Maqasid Shariah, as expressed by Muhammad Imarah,” he said.
“In the compassionate Madinatun Nabi (City of the Prophet), the poor are helped, the weak are cared for, and those who differ are given space. Monopolistic practices are rejected for a more equitable economic distribution, while envoys are sent out with a message to build a more peaceful and just order,” he added.
Anwar, who is also the Minister of Finance, said he always aspires for the best for all citizens and hopes that Allah SWT will continue to bless Malaysia and that its people will be bestowed with love and blessed sustenance.
In the same post, Anwar also shared the history and hardships faced by Prophet Muhammad SAW in establishing a new administration in the Arab region over 14 centuries ago.
“After a decade of exhausting reform efforts, Medina, which the Prophet nurtured with a just and compassionate order, successfully elevated the people with sound intellect and high moral character. Evidently, the Shariah paradigm transformed their personalities and minds with divine awareness and social maturity.
“The sharp clashes between the Aus and Khazraj tribes that had long shaken Yathrib were melted into the spirit of Ansar unity for the sake of stability, erasing the suspicion and anxiety that hindered progress,” he added.
He also shared a verse from Surah Quraysh, which translates to: “He who feeds them against hunger and secures them from fear.” — Bernama

Title: Anwar applauds Sukma 2026 champions, urges youth to chase glory and carry Malaysia’s name worldwide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and the state government for their commitment and hard work in successfully hosting the 2026 Malaysia Games (Sukma).
Anwar said the well-organised and vibrant staging of the Games demonstrated Selangor’s ability to host the country’s sporting event in a spirit of enthusiasm and togetherness.
He also congratulated the athletes, coaches, officials and secretariat involved, saying Sukma was not merely about winning medals but also a platform for discovering talent and producing champions.
“To our young people, continue striving and honing your talents because, God willing, some of you will one day carry Malaysia’s name on the world stage. Congratulations to all! Keep moving forward and continue bringing glory to the country.
“Congratulations also to Selangor’s Eliza Tan Ai Shen and Pahang’s Cheah Zen Hong, who were named the Best Female and Male Athletes, respectively. Even sweeter, hosts Selangor emerged as the overall champions of Sukma 2026,” he said in a Facebook post last night.
The Prime Minister also conveyed his deepest appreciation to the Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah for gracing the closing ceremony of the 22nd edition of Sukma.
In the same post, Anwar recalled that Sukma was launched 40 years ago following an idea conceived when he was Youth and Sports Minister in 1983.
“Today Sukma continues to serve as a platform uniting the talent, spirit and fighting determination of young people from across the country, including Brunei Darussalam,” he said. — Bernama

Title: IKEA picks Kuching for first-ever small store format in Malaysia, eyes December opening
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — IKEA Malaysia has confirmed that its first store in East Malaysia will open its doors in Kuching this December, marking a significant expansion into Sarawak after years of serving the state solely through e-commerce and delivery.
IKEA Malaysia revealed that the new outlet will be the retailer's first small-format store, building on IKEA's existing e-commerce and fulfilment presence in the state. IKEA Kuching will become the company's fifth physical store in Malaysia, joining IKEA Damansara, IKEA Cheras, IKEA Tebrau and IKEA Batu Kawan.
Unlike the brand's larger existing outlets, IKEA Kuching will adopt a small-format concept designed around convenience, allowing customers to browse room settings and home furnishing solutions while taking select products home the same day.
Shoppers will still have access to the wider IKEA catalogue for purchase, even if not everything is available for immediate pickup.
“We have heard from our customers in Sarawak, and we are excited that IKEA Kuching will soon be ready to welcome them,” said Malcolm Pruys, country retail director at IKEA Malaysia.
“Our ambition has always been to create a better everyday life for the many people. IKEA Kuching brings us another step closer to doing that by making the IKEA experience more accessible and relevant to how people here live at home.”
IKEA Malaysia also confirmed it is beginning to build its Kuching-based team ahead of the opening.
The company will engage with the local community to build its workforce, with an emphasis on creating growth opportunities for local talent.

Title: MetMalaysia warns of sustained hot spell, 17 areas nationwide placed under caution status
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) today issued a Level 1 (caution category) hot weather status for 17 areas across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said 11 of the affected areas are in Peninsular Malaysia, involving Larut and Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Kampar and Batang Padang in Perak; Kuala Krai in Kelantan; Kuantan, Raub, Temerloh and Pekan in Pahang; as well as Hulu Selangor and Gombak in Selangor.
Five areas in Sabah placed under the same status are Telupid, Tenom, Sandakan, Pitas and Beluran, while Marudi is the only affected area in Sarawak.
MetMalaysia said the Level 1 hot weather alert is issued when the maximum daily temperature in an area reaches between 35 and 37 degrees Celsius for at least three consecutive days.
The public can refer to MetMalaysia’s official website at https://www.met.gov.my/iklim/status-cuaca-panas/ for the latest daily hot weather updates nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Will Tian Chua contest Batu again? Returning PKR veteran eyes political revival
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Former PKR vice-president Tian Chua has set his sights on a return to Parliament and is open to contesting his former stronghold of Batu, citing enduring grassroots support from the constituency.
However, the 62-year-old stalwart maintained that any final decision regarding candidacy and seat deployment rests entirely with the party leadership.
“In the short term, of course, I think I still have the energy to contribute in Parliament, and I would like to go back to Parliament,” he told
FMT
in an interview.
Tian Chua represented Batu for two consecutive terms after winning the seat in 2008. He was barred from defending it in the 2018 general election after a returning officer disqualified his nomination papers over a RM2,000 court fine.
In response, he endorsed then independent student activist P. Prabakaran, who went on to secure the seat before formally joining PKR.
Tensions escalated during the 2022 general election when Tian Chua ran as an independent against Prabakaran after the party chose the incumbent to defend the seat, a move that led to Tian Chua's expulsion from PKR in January 2023.
Despite the political fallout, Tian Chua claimed that his ties to the grassroots remain intact.
“For the community in Batu, they have been expressing a strong desire that I would come back to serve them because I have been connected to them for a few decades now.”
Aside from his personal electoral prospects, the veteran politician stressed that his broader mission is ensuring PKR matures into an enduring democratic institution capable of outlasting individual political cycles.
“I think the main goal is that PKR wants to leave a legacy so that this political party’s name, Parti Keadilan Rakyat, is here to stay,” he said.
He urged the party to maintain its founding commitments to inclusivity and equality while cementing an institutional foundation that can weather shifting electoral tides.
Tian Chua drew comparisons to historic parties in established Western democracies, pointing to the UK's Labour, Conservative, and Liberal traditions that have endured for generations across shifting political fortunes.
“They go up and down,” he said, observing that such parties remain permanent pillars of their political ecosystems by representing foundational values and distinct societal segments.
He argued that PKR must strive for the same institutional resilience.
“So for me, that is the main thing that I hope to leave for the future generation,” he said.

Title: Police say Pasir Mas crash kills elderly woman and granddaughter, third victim hospitalised with injuries
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 25 — An elderly woman and her granddaughter were killed after the Perodua Axia they were travelling in veered off the road and crashed into a tree along Jalan Pasir Mas-Rantau Panjang near Culvert 5 in Pasir Mas yesterday.
In the 11.20 am incident, the 73-year-old woman, who was seated in the rear, died at the scene, while her 23-year-old granddaughter, who was seated in the front, died while receiving treatment at Pasir Mas Hospital.
Pasir Mas district police chief ACP Mazlan Hassan said the car was driven by another granddaughter of the victim, an 18-year-old girl, who suffered a fractured wrist and internal injuries and is receiving further treatment at the same hospital.
“The victims were three women from the same family, a grandmother and her two granddaughters, who were travelling from Pasir Mas towards Rantau Panjang,” he said in a statement today.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Police confirm Kajang road closures as Merdeka Eve celebration rehearsals roll out
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Five main roads around Kajang will be closed in stages from this Wednesday before being fully closed on Aug 30 in conjunction with the 2026 Selangor State Merdeka Eve Celebration at Kajang Stadium.
Kajang District Police Chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said the road closures were aimed at ensuring smooth traffic flow and public safety throughout the programme scheduled for Aug 30.
He said Jalan Mahkamah would be fully closed from Aug 26 to 30, while four other roads — Jalan Cempaka Putih, Jalan Cempaka Kuning, Jalan Stadium and Jalan Cheras — would be closed in stages.
“The staged closures for the rehearsals will be from 8.30 am to 10.30 am and 7 pm to 10 pm on Aug 28, as well as from 7 pm to 10 pm on Aug 29.
“All the roads involved will then be fully closed on the main day of the celebration, Aug 30, from 8 am until the event ends,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Naazron advised the public to plan their journeys in advance and use alternative routes to avoid traffic congestion around the celebration venue.
He said motorists were also urged to comply with instructions and guidelines given by police officers and personnel deployed at the scene.
To facilitate visitors, the organisers have also provided several designated parking areas around the celebration venue.
Visitors are also advised to use shuttle bus services provided from several major rail stations, including Sungai Jernih Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station, Bukit Dukung MRT, Jalan Bukit MRT, Jalan Reko Light Rail Transit (LRT) and Kajang 2 LRT.
Meanwhile, he said medical personnel and ambulances from Kajang Hospital, St John Ambulance, Kajang Plaza Medical Centre (KPMC) and the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) would be stationed at strategic locations to respond to any emergencies.
Members of the public with traffic-related enquiries or complaints can contact the Kajang District Police Headquarters (IPD) Control Centre at 03-8911 4222. — Bernama

Title: Ten arrested in Sandakan after woman found bound, murdered in home
Article:
SANDAKAN, Aug 25 — Police have arrested 10 suspects, including two primary individuals, following the brutal murder of a 62-year-old woman whose decomposing body was discovered bound inside a toilet in Tanah Merah, Jalan Leila, last Tuesday.
The victim, who lived alone in the two-storey wooden house, was found with her hands tied behind her back and her head covered with a cloth. Investigators believe she had been dead for several days prior to discovery, Sinar Harian reported.
Acting on a public tip-off regarding a foul stench emanating from the property, police responded to the scene at around 8.10pm and subsequently rounded up the 10 suspects in less than 24 hours.
Sandakan District Police Chief ACP George Abd Rakman confirmed the discovery.
“The discovery was made after police received information from the public at around 8.10pm regarding a foul smell coming from the house.
“The victim’s body was found decomposing and is believed to have been there for several days after she was killed,” he said in a statement.
George stated that the suspects, comprising five men and five women aged between 10 and 39, are all related to one another. Three are Philippine nationals, while the remaining seven are locals.
Initial interrogations revealed that the murder was triggered by a disagreement concerning payment for renovation works on the victim's house, alongside resentment over housing costs.
“The suspects were also believed to be dissatisfied after the victim increased the monthly rent for the house they were living in.
“Police also seized a wooden stick believed to have been used in the incident, as well as several personal belongings belonging to the victim that had been taken by the suspects,” George added.
The case is classified and investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, which carries capital punishment or lengthy imprisonment upon conviction.

Title: Selangor marks Sukma victory with Sept 1 holiday, honouring athletes and 10,000 volunteers
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 25 — The Selangor government has declared Sept 1 as a special holiday to commemorate the state contingent’s success in winning the overall title at the 2026 Malaysia Games (Sukma), held in Selangor.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari announced the decision at the Games’ closing ceremony at Aneka Walk, SA Sentral, here yesterday, adding that it was a token of appreciation from the state government to the entire Selangor contingent for bringing honour to the state.
“For the Selangor athletes, our children representing the red and yellow team, after 468 sporting events were contested, you successfully won 101 gold, 73 silver and 71 bronze medals.
“As the Selangor Menteri Besar, I am delighted with this remarkable performance. As a token of appreciation to every athlete and the 10,000 volunteers who contributed throughout the Games, I am pleased to announce that the Selangor state government has declared a special holiday to celebrate the Sukma 2026 victory, which will fall on Sept 1, 2026, next Tuesday,” he said in the presence of Raja Muda of SelangorTengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari, and 22nd Sukma and Para Sukma Organising Committee chairman, Selangor Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi.
He said the achievement also reflected the commitment and hard work of Selangor’s athletes, coaches and contingent officials in ensuring the state’s target at Sukma 2026 was achieved.
Amirudin also expressed his appreciation to all parties who supported the Selangor contingent throughout the Games.
“To everyone who has been with us since day one, I thank you for placing your trust in Selangor as the host of the 22nd Sukma and Para Sukma Games 2026.
“To the coaches and contingent heads, congratulations on your efforts to nurture talent and identify new athletes,” he said.
The Selangor contingent recorded a total of 101 gold, 73 silver and 71 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best performance when it first hosted the Games 28 years ago, as well as exceeding its target of 80 gold medals.
This marks Selangor’s 10th overall Sukma title, following victories in 1988, 1996, 1998, 2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2013 and, most recently, in 2016 in Sarawak. — Bernama

Title: Worth the bargain? Malaysian consumers win big on Pinduoduo as local sellers cry foul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 —Inside the sprawling digital storefront of Chinese e-commerce titan Pinduoduo, Shaun Kong routinely finds exactly what he didn't know he was looking for.
A few taps on his smartphone screen surface tailors recommendations for sports gear, from Formula 1 apparel to football jerseys.
For Shaun, who first encountered the platform while in China, its recent expansion into Malaysia was a welcome arrival. He uses it to purchase routine lifestyle items—clothing, accessories, and unbranded goods.
“To be honest, price is the biggest factor, and they do have quite a lot of variety,” he said, noting that the platform’s algorithm is surprisingly adept at serving hyper-specific consumer interests.
“Even the first time I went into the app, it already suggested football jerseys and F1 jerseys.”
Shaun is part of a fast-growing demographic of Malaysian consumers flocking to Chinese cross-border shopping platforms, including Pinduduo, which operates under PDD Holdings, the same corporate parent behind Temu, the international digital bazaar that built a global footprint on dirt-cheap prices and a steady stream of unbranded consumer goods.
Borrowing heavily from Temu’s high-volume, factory-to-doorstep model, Pinduoduo ships products directly from Chinese manufacturers to Malaysian consumers free of charge—even for orders as small as a single two-ringgit gadget, or about 45 cents.
And Pinduoduo has been relentless with social media advertisements, making itself highly visible in networks like Facebook to lure shoppers directly to factory-gate prices that undercut domestic retail by stark margins.
Another frequent shopper, who goes by the name Miky, noted that the platform has become a catch-all solution for non-urgent purchases.
“We’re getting winter stuff there with cheaper and more options to choose from, or hair clips, nice and cute stuff—literally everything,” Miky said, admitting that targeted social media ads showing discounts initially hooked her.
“You see it's cheap, so why not?”
For Miky, the trade-off comes down to patience. While local platforms like Shopee and Lazada offer next-day delivery on ready-stock items at higher price points, Pinduoduo shipments can take up to a month unless buyers opt for paid air shipping or bulk delivery surcharges.
"If you are buying stuff and you're not rushing to use it or need it, the quality actually isn't that bad, as long as you check the reviews," she added.
Is this Chinese dumping?
While Malaysian consumers celebrate the influx of bargain options amid living cost pressures, local business groups view the trend as a textbook manifestation of Chinese industrial overcapacity dumping, according to several news reports citing business owners and industry lobby groups.
Trade bodies, including the Malaysia Retail Chain Association and the Federation of Sundry Goods Merchants Associations of Malaysia, claimed domestic small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs) are facing severe margin compression.
Local storefronts and regional e-commerce vendors -- who bear the cost of local storefront rentals, inventory storage, tax compliance, and domestic workforce salaries -- say they are helpless to compete with cross-border factory-to-consumer models.
Items such as basic accessories or household tools often retailed locally for RM15 to RM50 can be found on Chinese cross-border apps for RM2, inclusive of direct overseas shipping.
Local merchant groups argue that this dynamic goes beyond standard free-market competition into predatory price distortion, accusing Chinese platforms of unloading oversupplied factory inventory abroad to sustain manufacturing output amid a slowing domestic economy.
Shipping time could edge Chinese pricing
Still, it's not an absolute defeat for Malaysian businesses, as shipping time remains a critical leverage point in consumer decision-making.
When urgency strikes, shoppers consistently tilt back toward local merchants. Malaysian consumers generally prefer to buy locally if the price markup remains reasonable, favoring immediate availability over waiting weeks for a cheaper shipment from China—even if the overseas option includes free shipping. For local retailers holding ready stock, speed and convenience serve as a crucial moat against cross-border price undercutting.
"If you need things immediately and you found them to be expensive in the shops, there are always Lazada and Shopee, which you can get like the next day if there are ready stock. And the prices are still cheaper compared to shops," said Miky.
This tension has pushed e-commerce from a consumer convenience into a hot-button policy debate in Putrajaya. Policymakers are increasingly worried that unchecked cross-border dumping risks gutting Malaysia’s SME sector, which forms the backbone of domestic employment and tax revenue.
To counter this, the Anwar administration introduced a 10 percent Low Value Goods (LVG) tax on imported online items under RM500, aiming to level the playing field between local retailers and foreign sellers.
Beyond tax measures, the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living is drafting a dedicated E-Commerce Bill to tighten oversight on foreign platforms, plug regulatory loopholes, enforce platform accountability, and mandate local representation for cross-border sellers.
But the divide remains sharp for now: while Malaysian shoppers embrace Chinese platforms for planned, low-cost purchases, domestic shopkeepers are left relying on speed, reliability, and upcoming policy interventions to survive in an increasingly borderless marketplace.
